Operator human-QA feedback: the expanded chart was hard to read. Browser observation showed the x-axis kit names were actually fine (horizontal, no truncation) -- the real defect was that NOTHING on the canvas stated what the bars measure. The y axis was bare numbers, the legend is off, and the word 'plates' appeared only in the hover tooltip; the description read 'Leader for This Month: sipes.edwina with 16' -- 16 of what. Fixed in UniqueScansLeaderboard only: added a chart subtitle 'Top 10 kits by unique plates - <window>', a y-axis title 'Unique plates', and the unit on both description lines. Also corrected interaction.mode from 'index'/intersect:false to 'nearest'/intersect:true -- that is a multi-series idiom inherited from RecoveryLeader/StagingLiveHitLeader, which plot kits x MONTHS, whereas this card is a single-series ranking. Extracted dateLabel() so the subtitle and the description cannot disagree about the window. The 'Leader for {label}:' prefix is deliberately preserved -- it is a house convention shared with both sibling leaderboards and is asserted on by tests/e2e/staging-live-hit-leader.spec.ts.

Follow-up to the readability fix: made the chart subtitle static after browser QA proved the windowed version went stale on a date-filter change (QF-8). Filament ChartWidget options are evaluated once at mount and painted to canvas; only the Blade description re-renders. Same one file, presentation only.

Added a 'Top kit - <window>' description to the COMPACT stat. The operator asked whether the card's number was the highest kit or a total; it is max() of the per-kit ranking, but nothing on the compact card said so -- a bare number above a sparkline of the ORG TOTAL (16 over a line ending at 84 on the QA fixture). The ticket body's 'definition wrinkle' clause requires that 'the card must be unambiguous about which it shows', so this is an UNMET TICKET REQUIREMENT, not polish. It sits outside the six enumerated ACs, which is why agent QA passed all six without catching it -- the ACs cover which number is computed and from where (the kit_id=0 rollup, never a sum: correct and verified), not whether the card SAYS which. Deliberately diverges from RecoveryLeader and StagingLiveHitLeader, which carry no such label: a recovery or a hit belongs to exactly one kit, so their per-kit values DO sum to their org total; only plate-uniqueness double-counts, which is precisely why the ticket singles this card out.

Emphasised the leader's bar in the expanded chart (same green, 0.85 fill + solid border) and muted the rest (0.3 fill + 0.5 border). The operator asked whether the top kit should be green and the others GREY; grey was declined with reason -- it is this dashboard's LOCKED signal (lockedStat() is ->color('gray'), getStatColor() falls back to grey, and a non-Pro org renders this whole card grey), so nine grey bars in a Pro-gated card would read as withheld rather than ranked lower. Staying inside the card's success green keeps its identity (shared with the scan family, DEV-2467 Q1) and its dark-theme contrast. Keys off the max VALUE rather than position, so every bar tied for top is emphasised -- with a tie, highlighting whichever kit sorted first would assert a ranking the data does not support. Presentation only.

Non-leader bars now use Filament's ACTUAL neutral grey -- `gray` resolves to Color::Zinc, so zinc-500 fill / zinc-400 border, copied verbatim from the framework palette rather than the green faded down. Operator corrected me twice here and was right both times: I had first reached for a horizontal-bar redesign (the labels were fine), then substituted a muted green for grey on the grounds that grey is the dashboard's locked signal. That objection does not survive checking -- lockedStat() never calls ->chart(), so a locked card renders NO bars at all and grey bars carry no locked-state meaning.

Compact card description now reads 'Top Kit: <name>' instead of 'Top kit - <window>'. The window is already on the page's own date filter; the kit behind the number was nowhere on the compact card. Naming it says 'this is ONE kit' more directly than any period label, and it removes the card's last duplicated window string -- the same drift surface that made the chart subtitle go stale (QF-8). The number and the name are now read from the SAME leader row, so they cannot describe different kits.

driver_verifications.method: (1) the implementing worker's original attribution; (2) the fix worker independently re-ran the broader CH+Dashboard directories repeatedly and saw at most 1 transient failure per run, always a DIFFERENT test, never one in this diff, each passing in isolation; it also restarted the clarity-qa-clickhouse container to rule out leaked memory and the flake persisted on a different test; (3) the driver's own AC-relevant run is clean at 84/84. Consistent with the known shared-literal-database contention documented in the clarity/testing knowledge card.

qa_findings.what: The non-Pro persona was seeded onto 'Padberg LLC', an OrgType::Client org. User::canAccessPanel() requires isRepo() && enable_genetech_hotlist for the app panel, so that persona hit a hard 403 on /app and could never reach the Company Metrics grid — making AC-6's locked state unverifiable in a browser.
qa_findings.fix: Created 'QA — Locked Repo Co' (Repo type, genetech enabled, NO COMPANY_METRICS entitlement) and moved persona 3 onto it; appended to .context/qa-seed.tinker.php so a re-seed keeps it. Verified: canAccessPanel=true, canViewCardData=false.

qa_findings.what: /__qa/login/{id} deliberately sets session('admin_impersonator') to mirror ImpersonateController. canViewCardData()'s documented bypass clause (Feature::active(...) || session()->has('admin_impersonator')) therefore grants every dev-login session automatic entitlement, so the LOCKED state of any COMPANY_METRICS-gated card cannot be observed through dev-login for any persona.
qa_findings.fix: None applied. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: UniqueScanCounts carried the identical bypass at base e469cf2d2, so this affects every Pro-gated card on every ticket and is not a DEV-2468 defect. AC-6 was instead verified in-process with the bypass cleared (Pro -> 16, non-Pro -> locked em-dash). Human QA through the real /app/login form is the way to see it rendered.

qa_findings.what: A ClickHouse MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (5.21 GiB container cap) surfaced through the Filament stats-overview widget during lane 2's filter cycling, cutting that lane short.
qa_findings.fix: docker restart clarity-qa-clickhouse dropped RSS 5.21 GiB -> 1.78 GiB; the seed survived and the card re-rendered correctly. NOTE: the card PROPAGATING a ClickHouse failure rather than swallowing it is DEV-2467's deliberate documented contract (a bounded-window failure must not persist a fabricated 0), so this is correct behaviour under an environment fault, not a defect.

qa_findings.severity: environment (not a defect, NOT this ticket's card)
qa_findings.what: Lane 2 saw ONE transient full-page 500 on /app: ClickhouseException 'memory limit exceeded' thrown from App\Filament\Widgets\Dashboard\RecoveryCounts::getModelQueryForDates() (RecoveryCounts.php:29) — a DIFFERENT card, not the Unique Scans Leaderboard. Did not recur across ~8 subsequent loads and filter clicks.
qa_findings.fix: None needed. Same root cause as QF-3: the shared local CH container under concurrent load from three parallel QA lanes hitting the dashboard at once. Restarting the container reclaimed 5.21 GiB -> 1.78 GiB. Not attributable to DEV-2468 — the failing card is untouched by this diff.

qa_findings.what: Lane 2 could not capture ANY screenshots: every agent-browser screenshot call (7+ attempts across fresh sessions, viewports and formats) hung or failed with 'CDP command timed out: Page.captureScreenshot' / 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)'. Lightweight reads (get text, snapshot, console, network) worked fine throughout, so the session was healthy — only the capture path failed, plausibly host GPU/Chrome contention from the three parallel lanes.
qa_findings.fix: None applied. Lane 2 substituted get-text reads, console/network inspection, and a direct tinker verification of the date-window math, so AC-3's evidence is complete despite the missing images. 9 screenshots exist from lanes 1 and 3.

_backstop_note: Backstop NOTES 1 and 2 were both WRONG (it assumed the card was being ADDED to cards(); it is already registered by DEV-2409 #394). Verified by grep: 16 ::class entries incl. 'unique-scans-leaderboard'. Its real value was surfacing tests/e2e/, which no candidate inventory listed.
